content: The test leaf shows: yellow/brown necrotic lesion at the tip/edge, scattered small dark spots on the surface, and a somewhat mottled appearance. Candidates: Bacterial_Spot, Septoria_Leaf_Spot, Late_Blight.

**Analysis of test image:**
- Tomato leaf on white background
- Large dark brown-black necrotic lesion at the left tip/edge with yellow-orange halo
- Small scattered dark brown spots on the remaining green portion
- Leaf is otherwise green

**Class comparison:**

- **Late_Blight**: Reference shows large dark brown-black irregular lesions at leaf margins with yellow halos — closely matches the main lesion at the tip
- **Early_Blight**: Shows dark lesions with yellow areas along edges, some concentric ring structure — similar but test image lacks clear concentric rings
- **Bacterial_Spot**: Smaller discrete spots with yellow halos; bottom-right reference shows yellow-brown margin but lesions are smaller than in test
- **Septoria_Leaf_Spot**: Small circular spots with dark borders — not matching the large lesion pattern
- **Verticillium_Wilt**: V-shaped yellowing pattern not visible; lesions don't match well
- **Other classes** (Mosaic, Powdery Mildew, Spider Mites, TYLCV, TMV): All show very different symptom patterns (mottling, white powder, curl/distortion) — ruled out

**Decision:** The dominant feature is the large, dark brown-black lesion spreading from the leaf tip with yellow-orange chlorotic halo — this is classic Late Blight (*Phytophthora infestans*). The scattered small spots are consistent with early lesions developing on the same leaf.
